text:
Model


state_names <- c(
  "S_C", "E_C", "I_C_pre", "I_C_post", "R_C",
  "S_H", "E_H", "I_H_pre", "I_H_post", "Q", "R_H",
  "cum_onset_C", "cum_onset_H", "cum_noso", "cum_adm_rash", "cum_inf_C"
)

measles_ode <- function(t, y, p) {
  S_C <- y[["S_C"]]
  E_C <- y[["E_C"]]
  R_C <- y[["R_C"]]
  I_C_pre <- y[["I_C_pre"]]
  I_C_post <- y[["I_C_post"]]
  S_H <- y[["S_H"]]
  E_H <- y[["E_H"]]
  R_H <- y[["R_H"]]
  Q <- y[["Q"]]
  I_H_pre <- y[["I_H_pre"]]
  I_H_post <- y[["I_H_post"]]
  
  beta_C   <- p[["beta_C"]]
  beta_H  <- p[["beta_H"]]
  xi_alpha <- p[["xi_alpha"]]
  alpha   <- p[["alpha"]]
  p_a      <- p[["p_a"]]
  p_i     <- p[["p_i"]]
  sigma    <- p[["sigma"]]
  eta     <- p[["eta"]]
  gamma <- p[["gamma"]]
  delta    <- p[["delta"]]
  delta_M <- p[["delta_M"]]
  
  ## ---- forces of infection
  N_C     <- S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C
  N_H_mix <- S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H
  
  lambda_C <- beta_C * (I_C_pre + I_C_post) / N_C
  lambda_H <- if (N_H_mix > 0) beta_H * (I_H_pre + I_H_post) / N_H_mix else 0   # no hospital: no ward infections
  
  ## ---- community
  dS_C      <- -lambda_C * S_C - xi_alpha * S_C + delta * S_H
  
  dE_C      <-  lambda_C * S_C - sigma * E_C - xi_alpha * E_C + delta * E_H
  
  ## I_C_pre leaves by four routes: rash onset splits three ways, plus general
  ## admission. The three onset coefficients sum to eta.
  dI_C_pre  <-  sigma * E_C -
    (1 - p_a) * eta * I_C_pre -          # -> I_C_post
    p_a * (1 - p_i) * eta * I_C_pre -    # -> I_H_post
    p_a * p_i * eta * I_C_pre -          # -> Q
    xi_alpha * I_C_pre +                 # -> I_H_pre
    delta * I_H_pre                      # <- I_H_pre
  
  dI_C_post <-  (1 - p_a) * eta * I_C_pre -          # <- I_C_pre
    gamma * I_C_post
  
  dR_C      <-  gamma * I_C_post - alpha * R_C + delta * R_H + delta_M * Q
  
  ## ---- hospital
  dS_H      <-  xi_alpha * S_C - lambda_H * S_H - delta * S_H
  
  dE_H      <-  lambda_H * S_H + xi_alpha * E_C - sigma * E_H - delta * E_H
  
  ## I_H_pre leaves by three routes: rash onset splits two ways, plus discharge.
  ## The two onset coefficients sum to eta.
  dI_H_pre  <-  sigma * E_H +
    xi_alpha * I_C_pre -                 # <- I_C_pre
    (1 - p_i) * eta * I_H_pre -          # -> I_H_post
    p_i * eta * I_H_pre -                # -> Q
    delta * I_H_pre                      # -> I_C_pre
  
  dI_H_post <-  (1 - p_i) * eta * I_H_pre +          # <- I_H_pre
    p_a * (1 - p_i) * eta * I_C_pre -    # <- I_C_pre
    gamma * I_H_post
  
  dQ        <-  p_i * eta * I_H_pre +                # <- I_H_pre
    p_a * p_i * eta * I_C_pre -          # <- I_C_pre
    delta_M * Q
  
  dR_H      <-  gamma * I_H_post + alpha * R_C - delta * R_H
  
  ## ---- cumulative trackers -------------------------------------------------
  dcum_onset_C  <- eta * I_C_pre          # all community rash onsets
  dcum_onset_H  <- eta * I_H_pre          # admissions, rash appeared AFTER arrival
  dcum_noso     <- lambda_H * S_H         # infections acquired as an inpatient
  dcum_adm_rash <- p_a * eta * I_C_pre    # admissions, rash present on arrival
  dcum_inf_C    <- lambda_C * S_C         # infections acquired in the community
  
  ## names are documentation: deSolve reads this by position, so the order must
  ## match state_names. The check below enforces that.
  list(
    c(
      S_C = dS_C,
      E_C = dE_C,
      I_C_pre = dI_C_pre,
      I_C_post = dI_C_post,
      R_C = dR_C,
      S_H = dS_H,
      E_H = dE_H,
      I_H_pre = dI_H_pre,
      I_H_post = dI_H_post,
      Q = dQ,
      R_H = dR_H,
      cum_onset_C = dcum_onset_C,
      cum_onset_H = dcum_onset_H,
      cum_noso = dcum_noso,
      cum_adm_rash = dcum_adm_rash,
      cum_inf_C = dcum_inf_C
    )
  )
}

Helpers.
p_i is fixed rather than estimated: it only changes how long I_H_post transmits, which the case series barely sees. It is varied in a sensitivity analysis instead.

p_i_fixed <- 0.9

init_state <- function(s_C0, s_H0, seed) {
  y <- c(
    S_C = s_C0 * N_C0 - seed, E_C = seed,
    I_C_pre = 0, I_C_post = 0, R_C = (1 - s_C0) * N_C0,
    S_H = s_H0 * N_H0, E_H = 0, I_H_pre = 0, I_H_post = 0, Q = 0,
    R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_H0,
    cum_onset_C = 0, cum_onset_H = 0, cum_noso = 0,
    cum_adm_rash = 0, cum_inf_C = 0
  )
  y[state_names]
}

## quantities implied by the sampled parameters
##   xi     odds ratio of susceptibility between hospital and community. This is
##          the value that makes s_C0 and s_H0 a fixed point of the disease-free
##          system, so the simulation starts without a transient.
##   alpha  admission rate for immune children, set so the population-weighted
##          rate equals the observed general admission rate alpha_bar.
##   D_inf  mean time a community case spends infectious. Cases admitted at rash
##          onset skip I_C_post, so this depends on p_a.
derived <- function(par) {
  s_C0 <- par[["s_C0"]]
  s_H0 <- par[["s_H0"]]
  
  xi       <- (s_H0 * (1 - s_C0)) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))
  alpha    <- alpha_bar / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
  xi_alpha <- xi * alpha
  
  a_C    <- (sigma + delta) / (sigma + xi_alpha + delta)
  D_inf  <- (1 + eta * (1 - par[["p_a"]]) / gamma) *
    (delta + eta * a_C) / (eta * (eta + xi_alpha + delta))
  beta_C <- par[["R_eff"]] / (D_inf * s_C0)
  
  list(
    xi = xi,
    alpha = alpha,
    xi_alpha = xi_alpha,
    D_inf = D_inf,
    beta_C = beta_C,
    beta_H = par[["kappa"]] * beta_C
  )
}

make_params <- function(par, d) {
  c(beta_C = d$beta_C, beta_H = d$beta_H,
    xi_alpha = d$xi_alpha, alpha = d$alpha,
    p_a = par[["p_a"]],
    p_i = if ("p_i" %in% names(par)) par[["p_i"]] else p_i_fixed,
    delta = delta, delta_M = delta_M,
    sigma = sigma, eta = eta, gamma = gamma)
}

solve_model <- function(par, times) {
  out <- tryCatch(
    ode(y = init_state(par[["s_C0"]], par[["s_H0"]], par[["seed"]]),
        times = times, func = measles_ode,
        parms = make_params(par, derived(par)),
        method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-6),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(out) || nrow(out) != length(times) || anyNA(out)) return(NULL)
  out
}

## weekly quantities. The two case types partition all rash onsets:
##   adm_w  = p_a * onset_C + onset_H   children admitted with measles
##   out_w  = (1 - p_a) * onset_C       community cases not admitted
run_model <- function(par, n_weeks, full = FALSE) {

  sol <- solve_model(par, seq.int(0L, n_weeks * 7L, by = 7L))
  if (is.null(sol)) return(NULL)

  onset_C  <- diff(sol[, "cum_onset_C"])
  onset_H  <- diff(sol[, "cum_onset_H"])
  adm_rash <- diff(sol[, "cum_adm_rash"])

  if (!full) {
    return(list(adm = adm_rash + onset_H,
                out = onset_C - adm_rash))
  }

  keep <- -1L   # drop t = 0, so each row pairs with one diff()

  tibble(
    week     = seq_len(n_weeks),
    onset_C  = onset_C,
    onset_H  = onset_H,
    adm      = adm_rash + onset_H,
    out      = onset_C - adm_rash,
    noso     = diff(sol[, "cum_noso"]),
    inf_C    = diff(sol[, "cum_inf_C"]),
    I_H_pre  = sol[keep, "I_H_pre"],
    I_H_post = sol[keep, "I_H_post"],
    Q        = sol[keep, "Q"],
    N_H      = rowSums(sol[keep, c("S_H", "E_H", "I_H_pre",
                                   "I_H_post", "Q", "R_H")])
  )
}

Parameters
Disease natural history (rate per day):

sigma <- 1 / 8      # exposed -> infectious
eta   <- 1 / 4      # pre-rash -> post-rash
gamma <- 1 / 4      # post-rash -> removed


Hospital population and alpha_bar
Number of children 15 years and under in HCMC:

N <- df_census |>
  filter(age <= 15) |>
  pull(n) |>
  sum()

cat("Total population N:", N)

Total population N: 1388365


Children’s Hospital 1 reported 90,000 admissions per year. Assume HCMC total is 5 times CH1, of which 40% are HCMC residents. Mean length of stay 5.2 days.
alpha_bar is admissions per community child per day, because in the ODE the admission flows multiply community compartments. Working from the admission count avoids needing N_C0 before alpha_bar is known, and makes the disease-free state balance exactly.

resident_frac <- 0.4
delta         <- 1 / 5.2

adm_per_day <- 5 * resident_frac * 90000 / 365
N_H0        <- adm_per_day / delta
N_C0        <- N - N_H0
alpha_bar   <- adm_per_day / N_C0

cat("admissions per day  :", round(adm_per_day), "\n")

admissions per day  : 493 

cat("hospital N_H0       :", round(N_H0), "=",
    round(N_H0 / (N / 10000), 1), "per 10,000 children\n")

hospital N_H0       : 2564 = 18.5 per 10,000 children

cat("community N_C0      :", round(N_C0), "\n")

community N_C0      : 1385801 

cat("balance: admissions", round(alpha_bar * N_C0, 1),
    " discharges", round(delta * N_H0, 1), "per day\n")

balance: admissions 493.2  discharges 493.2 per day


For comparison, HCMC reports 42 beds per 10,000 population. Applying the same 40% residency adjustment gives 16.8 per 10,000.


p_a and the instantaneous-admission assumption
The model admits a fraction p_a of community cases at rash onset, with no delay. That is justified only if the observed onset-to-admission interval is short. HCMC records a median of 0 days; the Hanoi line list is shown here for comparison.

Structural check
Confirms the derivative vector comes back in the order state_names expects and that the population is conserved. It has to run after the constants above, because derived and init_state read them.

  par <- c(R_eff = 1.3, kappa = 0.5, p_a = 0.1,

  d   <- measles_ode(0, init_state(0.08, 0.293, 10),
                     make_params(par, derived(par)))[[1]]

title: Result 3: Hospital-community model
text:
Disease-free equilibrium check
With transmission switched off, hospital occupancy and hospital susceptibility must stay flat. Drift means the inputs are inconsistent and every fit inherits an artificial transient.

disease_free <- function(s_C0 = 0.08, s_H0 = 0.293, days = 365) {

  par <- c(R_eff = 1.3, kappa = 0, p_a = 0.1,
           s_C0 = s_C0, s_H0 = s_H0, seed = 0)

  p <- make_params(par, derived(par))
  p[["beta_C"]] <- 0          # no transmission
  p[["beta_H"]] <- 0

  ode(y = init_state(s_C0, s_H0, 0), times = 0:days,
      func = measles_ode, parms = p,
      method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-6) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(
      day = time,
      N_H = S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + Q + R_H,
      s_H = S_H / (S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H),
      s_C = S_C / (S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C)
    )
}

text:
Calibration
Epidemic curve by inpatient and outpatient:

df_week_wide <- df_hcmc |>
  filter(age <= 15) |>
  mutate(
    date = as_date(ngay_nv),
    week = floor_date(date, "week", week_start = 1),
    type = if_else(inpatient, "inpatient", "outpatient")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(week), !is.na(type)) |>
  count(week, type, name = "cases") |>
  complete(week = seq(min(week), max(week), by = "week"), type,
           fill = list(cases = 0)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = cases, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(total = inpatient + outpatient,
         prop_inpatient = inpatient / total) |>
  arrange(week)

n_lead_weeks <- 8      # simulated weeks before the first observed week

obs <- df_week_wide |>
  arrange(week) |>
  mutate(t_week = row_number() + n_lead_weeks)

n_weeks   <- max(obs$t_week)
obs_idx   <- obs$t_week
obs_total <- obs$total
t0_date   <- min(obs$week) - 7 * (n_lead_weeks + 1)

n_total <- as.integer(sum(obs$total))
n_in    <- as.integer(sum(obs$inpatient))

cat("weeks:", n_weeks, " total:", n_total, " inpatient:", n_in,
    " share:", round(n_in / n_total, 3), "\n")

weeks: 88  total: 7114  inpatient: 3743  share: 0.526 



Likelihood
One reporting fraction rho applies to every case, admitted or not. Two terms:

weekly total reported cases
the inpatient share of all reported cases, as a binomial on the totals

Because the same rho scales both parts of the share, it cancels from q, so p_a is pinned by the observed share and rho by the level of the weekly series. Those are separate jobs, which keeps the two well identified.
One rho is also the right choice given that the September 2024 to March 2025 vaccination campaign is not in the model. A missing campaign inflates the number of infections the model needs, and rho is a free multiplicative scale that absorbs it. Because q is a ratio, p_a is protected: the campaign scales numerator and denominator alike. With two reporting fractions and rho_in fixed, the bias would land on p_a instead.
The cost of one rho is that admissions are taken to be as under-reported as everything else, so p_a comes out near the observed inpatient share.

par_names <- c("R_eff", "kappa", "p_a", "s_C0", "s_H0", "seed", "rho", "phi")

loglik <- function(x) {
  par <- setNames(as.numeric(x), par_names)

  sim <- run_model(par, n_weeks)
  if (is.null(sim)) return(-Inf)

  adm <- sim$adm[obs_idx]
  out <- sim$out[obs_idx]

  ## weekly total reported cases
  mu <- par[["rho"]] * (adm + out)
  ll <- sum(dnbinom(obs_total, mu = mu, size = par[["phi"]], log = TRUE))

  ## inpatient share of reported cases. rho cancels here by construction.
  # q <- sum(adm) / (sum(adm) + sum(out))
  # q <- min(max(q, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  # ll <- ll + dbinom(n_in, n_total, q, log = TRUE)

  if (is.finite(ll)) ll else -Inf
}



Prior

lower <- c(R_eff = 1.05, kappa = 0,  p_a = 0.005, s_C0 = 0.01,
           s_H0 = 0.05, seed = 1, rho = 0.001, phi = 0.1)

upper <- c(R_eff = 5,    kappa = 10, p_a = 0.90,  s_C0 = 0.40,
           s_H0 = 0.70, seed = 50, rho = 1, phi = 100)

n_C_eff <- 200    # effective n for s_C0: registry completeness, not registry size
n_H_eff <- 75     # effective n for s_H0: number of residual sera

log_prior <- function(x) {
  par <- setNames(as.numeric(x), par_names)

  dunif(par[["R_eff"]], 1.05, 5, log = TRUE) +
    dunif(par[["kappa"]], 0, 20, log = TRUE) +
    dbeta(par[["p_a"]], 2, 5, log = TRUE) +        # mean 0.29, deliberately wide
    dbeta(par[["s_C0"]], 0.2 * n_C_eff, 0.8 * n_C_eff, log = TRUE) +
    dbeta(par[["s_H0"]], 0.3 * n_H_eff, 0.7 * n_H_eff, log = TRUE) +
    dunif(par[["seed"]], 1, 50, log = TRUE) +
    dbeta(par[["rho"]], 2, 8, log = TRUE) +
    dunif(par[["phi"]], 0.1, 100, log = TRUE)
}

## draw from the prior, not from the bounding box, so the DEzs archive starts
## where the prior has weight
prior_sampler <- function(n = 1) {
  m <- cbind(runif(n, 1.05, 5), runif(n, 0, 20), rbeta(n, 2, 5),
             rbeta(n, 0.2 * n_C_eff, 0.8 * n_C_eff),
             rbeta(n, 0.3 * n_H_eff, 0.7 * n_H_eff),
             runif(n, 1, 50), rbeta(n, 2, 8), runif(n, 0.1, 100))
  if (n == 1) as.numeric(m) else m
}

prior <- createPrior(density = log_prior, sampler = prior_sampler,
                     lower = lower, upper = upper)



Starting point
R_eff follows from the observed growth rate alone: substituting the growth-rate solution for beta_C into R_eff = beta_C * D_inf * s_C0 cancels s_C0. Only a fraction 1 - p_a of pre-rash cases reach I_C_post, which is why that factor appears in the denominator. p_a starts at the observed inpatient share, which is where a single rho puts it.

# r_obs <- 0.0224      # refit over the actual growth phase
# 
# p_a_0   <- n_in / n_total
# D_0     <- 1 / eta + (1 - p_a_0) / gamma
# R_eff_0 <- (r_obs + sigma) * (r_obs + eta) * (r_obs + gamma) * D_0 /
#            (sigma * ((r_obs + gamma) + (1 - p_a_0) * eta))

weekly_counts <- function(data) {
  data |>
    count(week, name = "cases") |>
    complete(week = seq(min(week), max(week), by = "week"),
             fill = list(cases = 0L))
}

find_outbreaks <- function(data, threshold = ob_threshold,
                           min_run = ob_min_run, max_gap = ob_max_gap) {
  wc  <- weekly_counts(data)
  r   <- rle(wc$cases >= threshold)
  end <- cumsum(r$lengths)
  hit <- which(r$values & r$lengths >= min_run)

  if (length(hit) == 0) {
    return(tibble(episode = integer(), start = wc$week[0], end = wc$week[0],
                  weeks = integer(), cases = integer()))
  }

  s <- (end - r$lengths + 1L)[hit]
  e <- end[hit]

  tibble(s, e, grp = cumsum(c(1L, (s[-1] - head(e, -1) - 1L) >= max_gap))) |>
    summarise(i1 = min(s), i2 = max(e), .by = grp) |>
    transmute(
      episode = row_number(),
      start   = wc$week[i1],
      end     = wc$week[i2],
      weeks   = i2 - i1 + 1L,
      cases   = map2_int(i1, i2, \(a, b) sum(wc$cases[a:b])),
      peak_week  = map2_vec(i1, i2, \(a, b) wc$week[a:b][which.max(wc$cases[a:b])]),
      peak_cases = map2_int(i1, i2, \(a, b) max(wc$cases[a:b]))
    )
}

      rate_ma = slide_mean(rate, before = n_days - 1, complete = TRUE),
      .by = {{ group }}

pad_to <- function(g, target) {
  need <- target - ncol(g)
  if (need <= 0) return(g)
  pos <- max(pan_l(g))
  w   <- rep(list(gap, unit(1, "null")), length.out = need)
  if (need %% 2 == 1) w[[need]] <- unit(0, "cm")
  for (i in seq_len(need)) {
    g   <- gtable_add_cols(g, w[[i]], pos)
    pos <- pos + 1
  }
  g
}

# ---- Helpers --------------------------------------------------------
prev_correct <- function(est_val, sens, spec) {
  (est_val + spec - 1) / (sens + spec - 1)
}

clamp01 <- function(x) pmin(pmax(x, 0), 1)

# Vectorised prop.test CI (Wilson score with continuity correction)
prop_ci <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  z     <- qnorm((1 + conf) / 2)
  est   <- x / n
  yates <- pmin(0.5, abs(x - n / 2))
  z22n  <- z^2 / (2 * n)
  pc_u  <- est + yates / n
  pc_l  <- est - yates / n
  su    <- pmin(pc_u, 1)
  sl    <- pmax(pc_l, 0)
  tibble(
    ci_lwr = if_else(pc_l <= 0, 0,
                     clamp01((sl + z22n - z * sqrt(sl * (1 - sl) / n + z22n / (2 * n))) / (1 + 2 * z22n))),
    ci_upr = if_else(pc_u >= 1, 1,
                     clamp01((su + z22n + z * sqrt(su * (1 - su) / n + z22n / (2 * n))) / (1 + 2 * z22n)))
  )
}

predict_ci <- function(model, data, var, ci = 0.95, n_grid = 200) {
  link_inv <- model$family$linkinv
  df_res   <- nrow(data) - length(model$coefficients)
  tq       <- qt(1 - (1 - ci) / 2, df_res)
  rng      <- range(data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
  newd     <- tibble(!!var := seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = n_grid))
  pr       <- predict(model, newdata = newd, se.fit = TRUE, type = "link")
  newd |>
    mutate(
      fit = link_inv(pr$fit),
      lwr = link_inv(pr$fit - tq * pr$se.fit),
      upr = link_inv(pr$fit + tq * pr$se.fit)
    )
}

  d |>

                  .names = "{.col}_true"))

# Normal on the logit scale for the VE proportions (keeps draws inside (0,1),
# which matters at 99.6%), log scale for the reversion rate (keeps it
# positive). VE depends on dose count, not a product across doses, because the
# MCV2 estimate is a two-dose effectiveness.
# NOTE the 9-11 mo CI is asymmetric on the logit scale, so centring on the best
# estimate gives a sampled interval of about (66%, 94%) against the reported
# (72%, 95%): wider and lower, so conservative.
ci_sd <- function(lo, hi, trans) (trans(hi) - trans(lo)) / 3.92

draws <- tibble(
  ve1_L = plogis(rnorm(m_draws, qlogis(0.840), ci_sd(0.720, 0.950, qlogis))),
  ve1_H = plogis(rnorm(m_draws, qlogis(0.925), ci_sd(0.848, 0.970, qlogis))),
  ve2   = plogis(rnorm(m_draws, qlogis(0.996), ci_sd(0.993, 0.998, qlogis))),
  p_rev = exp(rnorm(m_draws, log(0.0022), ci_sd(0.0017, 0.0028, log)))
)

q_wk <- -log1p(-draws$p_rev) * 7 / 365.25   # weekly decay from annual reversion

draws |>                                    # sampled vs reported intervals
  summarise(across(everything(),
                   list(med = median,
                        lo = \(x) quantile(x, 0.025),
                        hi = \(x) quantile(x, 0.975))))

# Each child contributes one interval, so counting is a +1/-1 event table plus
# a cumsum: O(children), not O(children x weeks). key adds a dose-week
# dimension, which is what lets
#   sum_i VE_i(w) = mult * exp(-q w) * sum_s N[w, s] exp(q s)
# be evaluated with two small matrix products per term instead of m_draws
# passes over the registry.
count_intervals <- function(a, b, g, ng, key = rep(1L, length(a))) {
  a  <- pmax(a, 1L)
  b  <- pmin(b, n_week)
  ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b) & !is.na(g) & !is.na(key) & b >= a
  if (!any(ok)) return(list(n = matrix(0, n_week, ng), z = 0L, nk = 1L))
  a <- a[ok]; b <- b[ok]; g <- g[ok]; key <- key[ok]

  z   <- min(key):max(key)
  nk  <- length(z)
  nb  <- ng * nk * (n_week + 1L)
  off <- ((g - 1L) * nk + (key - z[1L])) * (n_week + 1L)
  d   <- tabulate(off + a, nb) - tabulate(off + b + 1L, nb)

  n <- matrix(d, nrow = n_week + 1L) |> apply(2, cumsum)
  list(n = n[seq_len(n_week), , drop = FALSE], z = z, nk = nk)
}

cover <- function(a, b, g, ng) count_intervals(a, b, g, ng)$n

term_matrices <- function(a, b, g, key, mult, ng) {
  kc <- count_intervals(a, b, g, ng, key)
  Ez <- exp(outer(kc$z, q_wk))                 # n_key  x M
  Ew <- exp(outer(seq_len(n_week), -q_wk))     # n_week x M
  map(seq_len(ng), \(gg) {
    cols <- ((gg - 1L) * kc$nk + 1L):(gg * kc$nk)
    (kc$n[, cols, drop = FALSE] %*% Ez) * Ew * rep(mult, each = n_week)
  })
}

build_series <- function(grp) {
  lev <- levels(droplevels(grp))
  ng  <- length(lev)
  gi  <- as.integer(factor(as.character(grp), levels = lev))

  mk <- function(entry, exit, vax, dose_lab) {
    b   <- wk_ge(exit) - 1L
    a_d <- wk_ge(entry)
    a_n <- pmax(a_d, wk_ge(vax))      # doses before entry count from entry
    tibble(
      week    = rep(weeks, times = ng),
      region  = rep(lev, each = n_week),
      dose    = dose_lab,
      n_denom = as.vector(cover(a_d, b, gi, ng)),
      n_vax   = as.vector(cover(a_n, b, gi, ng))
    )
  }

  cov_df <- bind_rows(
    mk(child$t9,  child$t60, child$d1, "Dose 1"),
    mk(child$t18, child$t60, child$d2, "Dose 2")
  ) |>
    mutate(region = factor(region, levels = lev),
           coverage = if_else(n_denom > 0, n_vax / n_denom, NA))

  numM <- replicate(ng, matrix(0, n_week, m_draws), simplify = FALSE)
  for (bb in 1:2) {                                   # single-dose periods
    sel <- which(!is.na(s_first) & band_first == bb)
    if (length(sel)) numM <- Map(`+`, numM, term_matrices(
      pmax(a_den, s_first)[sel], b_one[sel], gi[sel], s_first[sel],
      if (bb == 1L) draws$ve1_L else draws$ve1_H, ng))
  }
  sel <- which(!is.na(s_second))                      # two-dose periods
  if (length(sel)) numM <- Map(`+`, numM, term_matrices(
    pmax(a_den, s_second)[sel], b_exit[sel], gi[sel], s_second[sel],
    draws$ve2, ng))

  denE <- cover(a_den, b_exit, gi, ng)

  evc_df <- map2(seq_len(ng), lev, \(gg, nm) {
    E  <- numM[[gg]] / na_if(denE[, gg], 0L)
    qs <- apply(E, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
    tibble(week = weeks, region = nm,
           evc = qs[1, ], evc_lo = qs[2, ], evc_hi = qs[3, ])
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(region = factor(region, levels = lev))

  idx <- which(weeks >= win_start & weeks <= win_end)

  evc_win <- map2(seq_len(ng), lev, \(gg, nm) {
    dsum <- sum(denE[idx, gg])
    pa   <- if (dsum > 0) colSums(numM[[gg]][idx, , drop = FALSE]) / dsum
            else rep(NA_real_, m_draws)
    w <- evc_df$evc[evc_df$region == nm & between(evc_df$week, win_start, win_end)]
    tibble(region = nm,
           x     = median(pa),
           xu_lo = unname(quantile(pa, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)),
           xu_hi = unname(quantile(pa, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)),
           x_lo  = min(w, na.rm = TRUE),
           x_hi  = max(w, na.rm = TRUE))
  }) |>
    list_rbind()

  cov_win <- cov_df |>
    filter(between(week, win_start, win_end), n_denom > 0) |>
    summarise(x = sum(n_vax) / sum(n_denom),
              x_lo = min(coverage), x_hi = max(coverage),
              .by = c(region, dose)) |>
    mutate(xu_lo = NA_real_, xu_hi = NA_real_)

  list(cov = cov_df, evc = evc_df, cov_win = cov_win, evc_win = evc_win)
}

# are not independent tests. cor.test() gives the exact p when there are no
# ties; the normal approximation (exact = FALSE) is poor at n = 5.
cor_inc <- dat_inc |>
  summarise(
    n   = sum(is.finite(x) & is.finite(inc)),
    rho = if (n >= 3) cor(x, inc, method = "spearman",
                          use = "complete.obs") else NA_real_,
    p   = if (n >= 3) suppressWarnings(
            cor.test(x, inc, method = "spearman")$p.value
          ) else NA_real_,
    .by = c(metric, period)
  )

cor_inc

# For the figure legend: Spearman rho (p) by metric and period
cor_inc |>
  mutate(val = sprintf("%.2f (p = %.2f)", rho, p)) |>
  select(metric, period, val) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = val)

# rho label centred above each period's group of points
cor_lab <- dat_inc |>
  summarise(inc = (min(inc) + max(inc)) / 2, .by = c(metric, period)) |>
  left_join(cor_inc, by = join_by(metric, period)) |>
  mutate(lab = sprintf("rho = %.2f", rho))

# Fractional logit (quasibinomial GLM, logit link): the fitted curve stays
# inside 0-1 and bends near the bounds. Two parameters, like a straight line.
# Unlike Theil-Sen it is not robust to one outlying region.
fit_frac <- function(inc, x) {
  ok <- is.finite(inc) & is.finite(x)
  if (sum(ok) < 3) return(NULL)
  b    <- unname(coef(glm(x[ok] ~ inc[ok], family = quasibinomial)))
  grid <- seq(min(inc[ok]), max(inc[ok]), length.out = 100)
  tibble(inc = grid, x = plogis(b[1] + b[2] * grid))
}

fit_curve <- dat_inc |> reframe(fit_frac(inc, x), .by = c(metric, period))

# One panel per metric, x shared across panels. Colour = region, shape =
# period. Horizontal bars: exact 95% Poisson CI for incidence. Vertical bars:
# 95% VE-parameter interval (EVC) or exact 95% CI (seroprevalence); coverage
# is a registry census and carries no bar. Dashed curves: fractional logit fit
# per period.
p_inc_all <- ggplot(dat_inc, aes(inc, x, colour = region)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = inc_lo, xend = inc_hi, y = x, yend = x)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = inc, xend = inc, y = x_lo, yend = x_hi), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = period)) +
  # group = period keeps the three curves in a panel from joining up
  geom_line(data = fit_curve, aes(inc, x, group = period), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = cor_lab, aes(inc, y = Inf, label = lab),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", vjust = 1.3) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ ., scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_region) +
  # space above the points for the rho labels
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Cumulative incidence per 100,000", y = NULL,
       colour = "Region", shape = "Cases up to") +
  theme_epi +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", legend.position = "right")

p_inc_all

# 14. UNDER-5 CUMULATIVE INCIDENCE BY REGION

# The all-age version compares child immunity against an outbreak measured in

# children makes the incidence measure match what the immunity measures

case_age_lo <- 0     # years, inclusive
case_age_hi <- 5     # years, exclusive
 
# Setting case_age_lo <- 1 excludes infants, who are not yet MCV1-eligible and
# so sit outside the coverage and EVC denominators (9-59 months). That is the
# cleaner age match; 0-5 keeps the group epidemiologically complete.
 
dedupe_cases <- TRUE
 
# ---- duplicate records ----------------------------------------------------
 
df_ep2 |> summarise(rows = n(), unique_ids = n_distinct(id))
df_ep2 |> count(id) |> filter(n > 1) |> nrow()
 
# ---- census denominator ---------------------------------------------------
# Census age band k covers [k-1, k), so under 5 is bands 1:5, not 1:4.
 
census_u5 <- df_census |>
  filter(age >= case_age_lo + 1, age <= case_age_hi) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = district) |>
  mutate(district = merge_thuduc(clean_district(district)),
         region   = assign_region(district)) |>
  summarise(n_census = sum(n), .by = region) |>
  drop_na(region)
 
census_u5
 
# sanity: under-5s should be a few percent of the all-age total
tibble(u5 = sum(census_u5$n_census), all_age = sum(df_census$n)) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * u5 / all_age)
 
# ---- case numerator -------------------------------------------------------
 
cases_u5 <- df_ep2 |>
  (\(d) if (dedupe_cases) distinct(d, id, .keep_all = TRUE) else d)() |>
  filter(age >= case_age_lo, age < case_age_hi) |>
  mutate(district = merge_thuduc(.data[[col_district]]),
         region   = assign_region(district),
         date     = .data[[col_date]]) |>
  drop_na(region, date)
 
cases_u5 |> count(region)
cat("under-5 cases:", nrow(cases_u5), "of", nrow(df_ep2), "rows\n")
 
# ---- quarterly cumulative incidence ---------------------------------------
# Bins built from the full date range so the under-5 and all-age versions
# share a bin grid; regions with no cases in a quarter still get a row.
 
date_rng <- range(df_ep2[[col_date]], na.rm = TRUE)
bin_grid <- seq(floor_date(date_rng[1], "quarter"),
                floor_date(date_rng[2], "quarter"), by = "quarter")
 
inc_u5 <- cases_u5 |>
  mutate(bin = floor_date(date, "quarter")) |>
  count(region, bin) |>
  complete(region = census_u5$region, bin = bin_grid, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  arrange(region, bin) |>
  mutate(cum_n = cumsum(n), .by = region) |>
  left_join(census_u5, by = "region") |>
  mutate(
    group  = as.character(region),
    inc    = cum_n / n_census * 1e5,
    inc_lo = qchisq(0.025, 2 * cum_n) / 2 / n_census * 1e5,
    inc_hi = qchisq(0.975, 2 * (cum_n + 1)) / 2 / n_census * 1e5

inc_u5 |> select(group, bin, cum_n, n_census, inc) |> arrange(bin) |> print(n = Inf)

# ===========================================================================

bin_keep <- as.Date(c("2024-07-01", "2024-10-01", "2025-01-01",

bin_lab  <- setNames(format(bin_keep, "%b %Y"), as.character(bin_keep))
 
dat_u5 <- x_all |>
  inner_join(inc_u5 |> filter(bin %in% bin_keep) |>
               select(group, bin, region, inc, inc_lo, inc_hi),

         region = factor(as.character(region), levels = rank_order),
         bin    = factor(bin_lab[as.character(bin)], levels = unname(bin_lab)))
 
dat_u5 |> summarise(n = n(), .by = c(metric, bin)) |> print(n = Inf)
 
# ---- Spearman rho ---------------------------------------------------------
# Five regions per panel, and the six bins are nested cumulative counts, so
# read each row as a trajectory rather than as six independent tests.
 
cor_u5 <- dat_u5 |>
  summarise(
    n   = sum(is.finite(x) & is.finite(inc)),
    rho = if (n[1] >= 3) cor(x, inc, method = "spearman",
                             use = "complete.obs") else NA_real_,
    p   = if (n[1] >= 3) suppressWarnings(
            cor.test(x, inc, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$p.value
          ) else NA_real_,
    .by = c(metric, bin)
  ) |>
  mutate(lab = if_else(is.na(rho), "rho = NA",
                       sprintf("rho = %.2f\np = %.3f", rho, p)))
 
cor_u5 |> print(n = Inf)
 
# side by side with the all-age version, if section 13 was run
if (exists("cor_inc_all")) {
  cor_inc_all |>
    select(metric, bin, rho_all = rho) |>
    left_join(cor_u5 |> select(metric, bin, rho_u5 = rho), by = c("metric", "bin")) |>
    print(n = Inf)
}
 
# ---- Theil-Sen line, consistent with a rank correlation -------------------
 
theil_sen <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  if (length(x) < 3) return(NULL)
  cb   <- combn(length(x), 2)
  dx   <- x[cb[2, ]] - x[cb[1, ]]
  dy   <- y[cb[2, ]] - y[cb[1, ]]
  keep <- dx != 0
  if (!any(keep)) return(NULL)
  b <- median(dy[keep] / dx[keep])
  tibble(a = median(y - b * x), b = b, x1 = min(x), x2 = max(x))
}
 
fit_u5 <- dat_u5 |>
  reframe(theil_sen(inc, x), .by = c(metric, bin)) |>
  transmute(metric, bin, inc = x1, inc_end = x2,
            x = a + b * x1, x_end = a + b * x2)
 
# ---- figure ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Horizontal bars: exact 95% Poisson CI for the incidence rate.
# Vertical bars: 95% VE-parameter interval (EVC) or exact 95% CI
# (seroprevalence). Coverage is a registry census and carries no bar.
# Dashed line: Theil-Sen fit, an aid to reading direction, not a model.
 
p_u5 <- ggplot(dat_u5, aes(inc, x, colour = region)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = inc_lo, xend = inc_hi, y = x, yend = x)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = inc, xend = inc, y = x_lo, yend = x_hi), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_segment(data = fit_u5, inherit.aes = FALSE,
               aes(x = inc, xend = inc_end, y = x, yend = x_end),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = cor_u5, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = lab),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.2,
            lineheight = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ bin, scales = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_region) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Cumulative incidence per 100,000 children under 5",
       y = NULL, colour = "Region") +
  theme_epi() +
  theme(strip.placement = "inside")

tidy_or <- function(m, keep = NULL) {
  ct  <- summary(m)$coefficients
  est <- ct[, 1]; se <- ct[, 2]
  sel <- !grepl("ns\\(|Intercept", rownames(ct))
  out <- tibble(term = rownames(ct)[sel],
                or = exp(est[sel]),
                lo = exp(est[sel] - 1.96 * se[sel]),
                hi = exp(est[sel] + 1.96 * se[sel]),
                p  = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est[sel] / se[sel])),
                n  = stats::nobs(m)) |>
    mutate(txt = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", or, lo, hi))
  if (is.null(keep)) out else filter(out, term %in% keep)
}

desc_out <- function(dat, v, outcome) {
  lv <- levels(dat[[v]])
  d <- dat |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[v]])) |>
    summarise(n_tot = n(), n_pos = sum(.data[[outcome]]), .by = all_of(v)) |>
    rename(level = 1) |>
    mutate(level = as.character(level))
  if (!is.null(lv)) d <- d |> arrange(match(level, lv))
  d |> mutate(term = paste0(v, level),
              cell = sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", n_pos, n_tot, 100 * n_pos / n_tot))
}

    mutate(a = replace_na(a, "1 (ref)")) |>
    transmute(Characteristic = paste0("  ", level), n_out = cell, Adjusted = a) |>

}

trajectory <- function(par, days = n_weeks * 7) {
  sol <- solve_model(par, 0:days)
  if (is.null(sol)) return(NULL)
  d <- derived(par)
  as.data.frame(sol) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(

      s_H      = S_H / (S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H),
      lambda_C = d$beta_C * prev_C,
      lambda_H = d$beta_H * prev_H

}

max_days <- 10 * 365   # safety cap, in days

run_scenario <- function(beta_C,
                         kappa,
                         p_a,
                         p_i,
                         s_C0,
                         s_H0,
                         seed,
                         los,
                         adm,
                         threshold = 1,
                         ...) {
  stopifnot(seed > threshold)   # otherwise the run stops at once
  
  N_H      <- adm * los
  N_C      <- N - N_H
  xi       <- s_H0 * (1 - s_C0) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))
  alpha    <- adm / N_C / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
  xi_alpha <- xi * alpha
  
  y0 <- c(
    S_C = s_C0 * N_C - seed,
    E_C = seed,
    I_C_pre = 0,
    I_C_post = 0,
    R_C = (1 - s_C0) * N_C,
    S_H = s_H0 * N_H,
    E_H = 0,
    I_H_pre = 0,
    I_H_post = 0,
    Q = 0,
    R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_H,
    cum_onset_C = 0,
    cum_onset_H = 0,
    cum_noso = 0,
    cum_adm_rash = 0,
    cum_inf_C = 0
  )[state_names]
  
  p <- c(
    beta_C = beta_C,
    beta_H = kappa * beta_C,
    xi_alpha = xi_alpha,
    alpha = alpha,
    p_a = p_a,
    p_i = p_i,
    delta = 1 / los,
    delta_M = delta_M,
    sigma = sigma,
    eta = eta,
    gamma = gamma
  )
  
  sim <- function(p) {
    ode(
      y0,
      0:max_days,
      measles_ode,
      p,
      method = "lsoda",
      rootfunc = make_stop_condition(threshold),
      atol = 1e-3,
      rtol = 1e-6
    )
  }
  final <- function(sol, x)
    sol[nrow(sol), x]   # value at the stop time
  
  sol  <- sim(p)
  sol0 <- sim(replace(p, "beta_H", 0))
  
  noso  <- final(sol, "cum_noso")
  inf_C <- final(sol, "cum_inf_C")
  D_inf <- 1 / (eta + xi_alpha) + eta / (eta + xi_alpha) * (1 - p_a) / gamma
  
  tibble(
    t_end     = final(sol, "time"),
    faded     = max(t_end, final(sol0, "time")) < max_days,
    R_eff     = beta_C * s_C0 * D_inf,
    noso_pct  = 100 * noso / (noso + inf_C),
    peak_prev = 1000 * max(sol[, "I_H_pre"] + sol[, "I_H_post"]) / N_H,
    inf_C     = inf_C,
    attr_C    = 100 * (inf_C - final(sol0, "cum_inf_C")) / inf_C
  )
}

## rate: ward infections per day that one infectious, non-isolated child
## spends on the ward
k_hh_parts <- function(beta_H, s_H0, los, p_i, p_a) {
  delta  <- 1 / los
  p_inf  <- sigma / (sigma + delta)       # becomes infectious before discharge
  p_rash <- p_inf * eta / (eta + delta)   # rash appears before discharge
  rate   <- beta_H * s_H0
  tibble(
    pre_rash  = rate * p_inf / (eta + delta),                   # before the rash
    post_rash = rate * p_rash * (1 - p_i) / gamma,              # rash on ward, not isolated
    readmit   = rate * (1 - p_rash) * p_a * (1 - p_i) / gamma,  # back with rash, not isolated
    K_HH      = pre_rash + post_rash + readmit
  )
}

## total infections, run to fade-out, for one set of conditions
total_infections <- function(beta_C, kappa, p_a, p_i, s_C0, s_H0, seed,
                             los, adm, threshold = 1, ...) {
  stopifnot(seed > threshold)   # otherwise the run stops at once
  
  N_H   <- adm * los
  N_C   <- N - N_H
  xi    <- s_H0 * (1 - s_C0) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))
  alpha <- adm / N_C / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
  
  y0 <- c(S_C = s_C0 * N_C - seed, E_C = seed, I_C_pre = 0, I_C_post = 0,
          R_C = (1 - s_C0) * N_C,
          S_H = s_H0 * N_H, E_H = 0, I_H_pre = 0, I_H_post = 0, Q = 0,
          R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_H,
          cum_onset_C = 0, cum_onset_H = 0, cum_noso = 0,
          cum_adm_rash = 0, cum_inf_C = 0)[state_names]
  
  p <- c(beta_C = beta_C, beta_H = kappa * beta_C,
         xi_alpha = xi * alpha, alpha = alpha, p_a = p_a, p_i = p_i,
         delta = 1 / los, delta_M = delta_M,
         sigma = sigma, eta = eta, gamma = gamma)
  
  sol <- ode(y0, 0:max_days, measles_ode, p, method = "lsoda",
             rootfunc = make_stop_condition(threshold),
             atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-6)
  last <- function(x) unname(sol[nrow(sol), x])   # value at the stop time
  
  tibble(total = last("cum_inf_C") + last("cum_noso"),   # infections after the start
         noso  = last("cum_noso"),
         faded = last("time") < max_days)
}

## ---- 2. kappa above which the hospital amplifies (the black line) ---------------
## linear interpolation between the last kappa below 0% and the first at or above;

kappa_amp <- function(kappa, net) {
  i <- which(net >= 0)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) return(NA_real_)
  if (i == 1) return(kappa[1])
  kappa[i - 1] + (0 - net[i - 1]) * (kappa[i] - kappa[i - 1]) / (net[i] - net[i - 1])
}

title: Result 3: Hospital-community model
text:
R0H and R0C validation
The simulation set everyone in the population susceptible, and introduce 1 infectious in the pre-rash state in the community (to check R0C), or hospital (to check R0H).

## ---- closed forms from the next-generation matrix ----------------------------
r0h_formula <- function(beta_H,
                        eta,
                        gamma,
                        delta,
                        xi_alpha,
                        p_a,
                        p_i) {
  k <- eta + xi_alpha + delta
  beta_H * ((eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * k) +
              (1 - p_i) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / k)
}

r0c_formula <- function(beta_C, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a) {
  k <- eta + xi_alpha + delta
  beta_C * (eta + delta) / k * (1 / eta + (1 - p_a) / gamma)
}

## ---- the same quantities from the model ODE -----------------------------------
## seed_in: compartment of the index child ("I_H_pre" or "I_C_pre")
## count:   which infections to count ("cum_noso" or "cum_inf_C")
## Everyone is susceptible, so S_C = N_C and S_H = N_H at the start.
simulate_new_infections <- function(beta_C,
                                    beta_H,
                                    eta,
                                    gamma,
                                    delta,
                                    xi_alpha,
                                    p_a,
                                    p_i,
                                    N_C,
                                    N_H,
                                    seed_in,
                                    count) {
  y0 <- c(
    S_C = N_C,
    E_C = 0,
    I_C_pre = 0,
    I_C_post = 0,
    R_C = 0,
    S_H = N_H,
    E_H = 0,
    I_H_pre = 0,
    I_H_post = 0,
    Q = 0,
    R_H = 0,
    cum_onset_C = 0,
    cum_onset_H = 0,
    cum_noso = 0,
    cum_adm_rash = 0,
    cum_inf_C = 0
  )[state_names]
  y0[seed_in] <- 1   # one infectious child
  
  p <- c(
    beta_C = beta_C,
    beta_H = beta_H,
    xi_alpha = xi_alpha,
    alpha = 0,
    p_a = p_a,
    p_i = p_i,
    sigma = 0,
    eta = eta,
    gamma = gamma,
    delta = delta,
    delta_M = 1 / 7
  )
  
  ## long enough for the index child to finish its infectious period
  t_end <- 50 / min(eta, gamma)
  
  out <- ode(y0,
             c(0, t_end),
             measles_ode,
             p,
             rtol = 1e-10,
             atol = 1e-10)
  out[2, count]
}

## ---- parameter sets -------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. the baseline values
baseline <- tibble(
  beta_C = 15 / 8,
  beta_H = 15 / 8,
  eta = 1 / 4,
  gamma = 1 / 4,
  delta = 1 / 5.2,
  xi_alpha = 0.001,
  p_a = 0.3,
  p_i = 0.9
)

## 2. the baseline with p_a and p_i at their limits (0 or 1)
edges <- baseline |>
  select(-p_a, -p_i) |>
  expand_grid(p_a = c(0, 1), p_i = c(0, 1))

## 3. random values over wide ranges
set.seed(2026)
n_random <- 200
random <- tibble(
  beta_C   = runif(n_random, 0.5, 5),
  beta_H   = runif(n_random, 0.1, 10),
  eta      = 1 / runif(n_random, 1, 7),
  # pre-rash infectious period, 1 to 7 days
  gamma    = 1 / runif(n_random, 1, 7),
  # post-rash infectious period, 1 to 7 days
  delta    = 1 / runif(n_random, 1, 30),
  # length of stay, 1 to 30 days
  xi_alpha = runif(n_random, 0.001, 0.01),
  p_a      = runif(n_random),
  p_i      = runif(n_random)
)

## population sizes
## N_C is very large, so that the infections caused by one child do not reduce
## the susceptible proportion. R_0H and R_0C do not depend on N_C or N_H.
## N_H = adm * los, with adm = xi_alpha * N_C admissions per day and
## los = 1 / delta. This makes admissions equal discharges, so the population
## sizes stay constant. xi_alpha must be above 0, otherwise N_H = 0.
pars <- bind_rows(
  baseline = baseline,
  edges = edges,
  random = random,
  .id = "set"
) |>
  mutate(N_C = 1e6, N_H = xi_alpha * N_C / delta)

## ---- compare -------------------------------------------------------------------
## pick() passes each row's parameters to simulate_new_infections() by name
check <- pars |>
  mutate(
    R0H_formula   = r0h_formula(beta_H, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a, p_i),
    R0H_simulated = pmap_dbl(
      pick(beta_C:N_H),
      simulate_new_infections,
      seed_in = "I_H_pre",
      count = "cum_noso"
    ),
    R0C_formula   = r0c_formula(beta_C, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a),
    R0C_simulated = pmap_dbl(
      pick(beta_C:N_H),
      simulate_new_infections,
      seed_in = "I_C_pre",
      count = "cum_inf_C"
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    starts_with("R0"),
    names_to = c("quantity", ".value"),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) |>
  mutate(rel_diff = simulated / formula - 1)

## the baseline and the four limit cases
check |>
  filter(set != "random") |>
  select(quantity, set, p_a, p_i, formula, simulated, rel_diff) |>

plot_check <- function(data, title) {

    geom_abline(slope = 1,

    scale_x_log10() +

    theme_classic(base_size = 11)
}
